newsitem.title: BULGARIA: HEIDELBERGER BUYS TWO BULGARIAN CEMENT PLANTS.
newsitem.headline: HEIDELBERGER BUYS TWO BULGARIAN CEMENT PLANTS.

text.p: Germany's Heidelberger Zement AG has bought 51 percent of Bulgaria's Zlatna Panega cement plant and 75 percent of the Granitoid-Pernik plant for a total of $27.5 million, Deputy Prime Minister Evgeni Bakardzhiev said.

"Bulgaria signed on Wednesday a preliminary agreement to sell 51 percent of Zlatna Panega for $26 million and 75 percent of Granitoid for $1.5 million to Heidelberger Zement AG," Bakardzhiev told a news conference.
The deals are expected to be finalised once parliament approves new amendments to the concession law allowing the cabinet to issue concessions, he added.

Under Wednesday's agreement Heidelberger will have to pay $19 million in cash and $7 million in domestic bad debt loan bonds known as Zunks or Bulgarian Brady bonds in 30 days after the Zlatna Panega deal is finalised.
The 75 percent stake in Granitoid will all be paid in cash in 30 days after the deal is finalised.
A Heidelberg official said he was optimistic about the future of the two plants.

"We believe that we will raise output significantly because Zlatna Panega has good potential and we are committed to fulfilling our investment obligations," said Heidelberg board member Walter von Glass.

Under the preliminary agreement, the new owner must invest a total of $25 million in Zlatna Panega, $15 million of that in the next three years under the condition that the sum will not be invested in a capital increase. Heidelberger must invest $3 million in Granitoid in the next four years. -- Sofia newsroom +359-2 981 4145
